instruction: Review the 2023 book reading spreadsheet on your desktop. Determine which genre appears most frequently in your reading list and write that genre in the 'book_list_result.docx' document.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 's'); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.explanation: Task requires finding the most common genre. Verified with Python: Genre counts are Science Fiction (3), Fantasy (2), and 7 other genres with 1 book each. The most common genre is Science Fiction. Evaluator checks if the DOCX contains 'Science Fiction'.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly extracts DOCX text content and checks for expected genre 'Science Fiction'
Postconfig properly saves the file (Ctrl+S) before verification to ensure latest content is read
Expected value 'Science Fiction' is semantically correct based on metadata analysis (3 occurrences, most frequent)
Getter logic is sound: reads correct file path (/home/user/Desktop/book_list_result.docx) and extracts all paragraph text
Metric logic works: performs case-insensitive substring matching to verify genre name appears in document
Minor issue: substring matching may be overly permissive (e.g., 'Not Science Fiction' would pass), though this is acceptable for document writing tasks where users might write full sentences

Minor limitation: evaluator only verifies final output (genre written in DOCX), not intermediate analysis steps (counting genres in spreadsheet), but this is standard for outcome-based verification in OSWorld tasks
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider adding exact match or more strict pattern matching if only the genre name alone should be accepted (e.g., using regex for word boundaries)
Consider verifying the spreadsheet was actually opened/accessed, though this may not be feasible with current getter capabilities
